REVIEW:
# Review: Order Online, Pick Up in Store Rollout Recommendation

This is a strong memo. It leads with a clear recommendation, takes apart the $54.8M headline with the pilot's own data, and builds a timeline around the real constraints: permits, the peak-season training problem and the Thanksgiving target. I checked the arithmetic, and nearly all of it holds. The issues below are mostly about labelling, unsupported figures and loose ends.

## Calculations verified

| Claim | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| $54.8M | 46 × $96 × 365 × 34 = $54,802,560 | ✅ |
| Delivery switchers +$2.44 | $8.64 fee − $6.20 picking | ✅ |
| In-store switchers −$9.28 | ($11 × 28%) + $6.20 | ✅ |
| New customers +$20.68 | $96 × 28% − $6.20 | ✅ |
| Blended ≈ $4 | 0.29(2.44) + 0.38(−9.28) + 0.33(20.68) = $4.01 | ✅ |
| ≈ $2.3M/year | 570,860 orders × $4.01 | ✅ |
| Payback > 2 years at half volume | $2.6M ÷ $1.15M ≈ 2.3 years | ✅ |
| Waves cover all stores | 8 + 12 + 11 + 3 pilots = 34; 23 no-permit stores − 3 pilots = 20 | ✅ |
| Thanksgiving Nov 25, 2027 | Fourth Thursday of November 2027 | ✅ (US) |

## Issues to fix

**1. "$15.7 million in genuinely new sales" is mislabelled.** 33% of $54.8M is $18.1M. The $15.7M figure only appears once you subtract the lost impulse sales (38% × 570,860 orders × $11 ≈ $2.4M). That is a reasonable net figure, but the COO cannot reproduce it from the text. A reader who multiplies 33% by $54.8M will think it is an error. Call it "net new sales, after lost impulse purchases," or use $18.1M.

**2. The $35 minimum order has no basis.** Nothing in the brief or the memo supports it, and the pilot economics point different ways depending on the customer:
- New customers break even at about $22 ($6.20 ÷ 28%).
- Delivery switchers break even at about $69 ($6.20 ÷ 9%).
- In-store switchers lose money at any basket size.

Either show how $35 was derived or describe it as a proposed starting point to test in Wave 1.

**3. The permit dates contradict each other.** The table says to file permits in January, but Wave 3 says permits arrive "3–5 months from February." Pick one. Filing in January gives April–June arrivals. The schedule also doesn't allow time for building the bays after permits arrive. Even so, Aug–early Oct probably still works.

**4. The May gate has no thresholds.** "Proceed only if results justify it" leaves the decision open. Give concrete triggers, for example at least 23 orders per day (half the pilot), at least $X contribution per order, and a substitution rate under Y%. The memo should also say what happens to the Thanksgiving target if the gate fails, and whether permit filings (already paid for) go ahead regardless.

**5. The union premium may not be in the cost model.** The memo mentions the $1.10/hour clerk premium but doesn't say whether the $6.20 picking cost already includes it. If it doesn't, every per-order figure is slightly overstated. One clause would settle this.

**6. The pilot stores are never mentioned in the timeline.** The waves cover 31 stores. Add a note that the 3 pilot stores continue, so the COO can see how the plan reaches 34.

**7. There is a stray empty heading at the end.** The document ends with `---` followed by an empty `##`. Delete it.

## Minor points

- **Which Thanksgiving?** The brief spells it "labour," which is Canadian usage. Canadian Thanksgiving 2027 falls on October 11, which would make the mid-October completion date too late. The holiday-season framing suggests the US date is intended, but confirm it.
- **Delivery context is unused.** The fact that delivery is 4.1% of sales could put the 29% cannibalization in proportion. This is optional and depends on the word budget.
- **Cost exclusions are buried.** "Before substitution costs, marketing and the $2.6 million investment" is an important caveat in the middle of a paragraph. Consider bolding it or moving it next to the $2.3M figure.
- **Length:** about 590 words, within the 450–600 target. Any additions (gate thresholds, the $35 rationale) will need cuts elsewhere. The Budget section could absorb some of them.

## Overall

The memo is ready to send once you fix items 1–4 and remove the stray heading. Items 1 and 2 matter most, because they are numbers the COO may check or challenge.
